components.title: Tabs
components.purpose: Horizontal section navigation. Chrome placement (below the plugin topbar) or card placement (sub-navigation inside a flush card).

api.label: Modifiers
items: .tabs--card (sub-navigation inside a .card--flush, below the card header; smaller type, underline hugs the label)
.tabs--boxed (same sub-navigation rung as --card, folder tabs that fuse into the panel below — stronger current-page anchor for dense screens)
.tabs--vertical (same rung, rail layout for a .columns two-column screen; current state is an accent-fill, not an underline)

.tabs--segmented (inline button-group control for a small 2-4 equally-weighted toggle, not a section list — the one variant that doesn't require a breadcrumb; square radius matches .button, not a pill shape)

api.label: Rules
items: At most one chrome .tabs strip per screen: it's the primary nav for a single menu-item plugin, or a page's section nav under the header when the sidebar submenu is primary (the WP settings-tabs pattern). Never two competing strips.
--card/--boxed/--vertical are page-level sub-navigation only; never use them in parallel with a chrome .tabs strip on the same screen, and never use two of them together.
In card placement the tab panel content goes in .card__body, directly after the tabs row.
--segmented is for interchangeable views of the same thing (Visual/Code, Day/Week/Month) — if the options are a section list instead, use --card/--boxed/--vertical or .subnav.
Composition: see the strip working as primary nav, and stacked with subnav and drill-in, in navigation patterns.

components.title: Subnav
components.purpose: Secondary navigation strip directly under whichever primary nav is in use — chrome tabs, or directly under .page-header when the sidebar submenu is primary: pages of a section (navigation level 2). Two variants — pick one.

api.label: Anatomy
items: nav.subnav.subnav--links|--tabs > __link — no pipes, no counts (those are the .views signature)

api.label: Modifiers
items: .subnav--tabs (block tabs filling the row; --current takes the canvas/body bg and drops the bar border to blend into the content below)

api.label: Rules
items: Navigation ladder: primary = sidebar submenu OR (single menu-item) a top-level chrome .tabs strip · secondary (max one) = chrome .tabs under the header (WP settings-tabs) OR .subnav OR the .tabs--card/--boxed/--vertical drill-in patterns · .views = filtering, not a nav level.
Default home: directly under the titled .page-header (full-bleed, outside any card) — never directly under another nav strip. A strip needs a title above it (the labeled-parent rule, heuristics §2b).

--links is the quiet default under a header. --tabs exists for one composition only — the bare direct stack fused under the chrome .tabs strip, which agents build on explicit user request only (heads-up about the anchoring cost, then comply). On the canvas under a header, the stronger-anchor option is .tabs--boxed, not --tabs.
Composition: the "tabs + subnav" and "submenu + page tabs" layouts are worked out in navigation patterns.

components.title: Section index
components.purpose: In-page table of contents for long settings pages (~2+ viewport heights): anchor links to the page's sections. Pure anchors + CSS — no JS. Not a nav level; it points inside the current page.

api.label: Anatomy
items: nav.section-index > __title + __list > li > __link — always an aria-labeled nav

api.label: Modifiers
items: .section-index__link--current (pair with aria-current="true"; dark bold — "colored = clickable, dark = you are here")

api.label: Rules
items: Optional, for pages exceeding ~2 viewport heights — shorter pages don't need one.
Static by default. --sticky only inside a .columns aside rail; the kit sets root scroll-padding-top so anchor jumps don't hide section titles, and links keep the visible keyboard focus.
Not a nav level: it coexists with any primary/secondary nav (like .views, it's orthogonal to the ladder).

Place directly above the list-table, inside the .card--flush after the card header.
